clue.text: Small creature, not unlike an antelope

blocks.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite
not unlike means like, which is the French-derived à la, as in à la mode

explanation.surface: A tiny animal that rather resembles an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unlike' reads as a vague comparison; its double negative simply means like, rendered as à la.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African antelope, and also the Chevrolet Impala, one of the grid's nine cars.

clue.text: Game is originally much different on International Workers' Day

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of much
different as in other
International Workers' Day falls on May 1, with I as the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A game played very differently on May Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother May I is a children's game in which players must ask permission before moving. 'on' places the first pieces above MAY I in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother May I is a traditional playground game, like Simon Says, in which a leader grants or refuses moves.

clue.text: Native American stirred Coke here

indicators.note: a stirred drink is mixed around, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Native American person stirs a glass of Coca-Cola at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the Jeep Cherokee, one of the grid's nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people originally of the southeastern United States.

clue.text: Look northward in Vermont unit

indicators.note: in a down entry, going northward means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
in means placed inside, so the reversed word sits within the state abbreviation

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
VT is the postal abbreviation for Vermont

explanation.surface: An instruction to glance north while inside a Vermont building unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the Chevrolet Volt, one of the nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The volt is the SI unit of electric potential difference.

clue.text: Think again about scone, chewed and swallowed by passenger

indicators.note: food that is chewed is broken up and mashed, so the letters are jumbled
whatever is swallowed goes inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the traveller

blocks.note: the letters of scone, rearranged
a passenger rides, so a rider

explanation.surface: A traveller munching a scone pauses to think again.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled scone goes just after the first letter of the traveller's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider a matter is to weigh it once more, perhaps changing one's mind.

clue.text: In Montreal, seven unprotected lice infested with bacteria

indicators.note: a word without protection has lost its outer covering, so its first and last letters go

blocks.note: sept is French for seven, and Montreal is French-speaking
the middle letters of lice

explanation.surface: In a Montreal report, seven unhygienic lice carry bacterial infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound or system is contaminated by bacteria and the infection they cause.

clue.text: Insect putting its head underneath a piece of paper

indicators.note: moving the head to the bottom of a down entry sends the first letter to the end

blocks.note: a flea is a small jumping insect

explanation.surface: A bug crawls headfirst under a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the Nissan Leaf, one of the grid's nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is a single sheet of paper in a book, as in turning over a new leaf.

clue.text: Draws carts bit by bit, with some repetition

indicators.note: taking something apart bit by bit breaks it into pieces that can be rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
some of the letters already used are repeated: an A and two Ts

explanation.surface: Someone sketches carts piece by piece, drawing some parts over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: the answer is spelt only with the letters of carts, with some of them used again, rather than a strict rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, as a magnet pulls in iron filings.

clue.text: Kiss faceless bum

indicators.note: a word without its face has lost its front, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a smooch is a kiss

explanation.surface: A rude instruction to plant a kiss on a backside with no face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like a noun for a backside, but here it is the verb meaning to cadge, and 'faceless' strips the S from SMOOCH to leave MOOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is to beg or cadge it, and to mooch is likewise to scrounge freely from others.

clue.text: Expend too much energy flipping dinosaur before edges of volcano

indicators.note: flipping something turns it end to end, so the whole string that follows is read backwards
the edges of a word are its outside letters, so only the first and last are kept

blocks.note: the T. rex, the best-known dinosaur
ere is an old word for before
the first and last letters of volcano

explanation.surface: Someone wears themselves out turning a dinosaur over near the rim of a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a link word ordering the pieces, but it is the old word ere; 'flipping' then applies to the whole string, not just the dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert yourself is to push your body past its limit, spending more effort than is wise.

clue.text: Marshall Mathers' college

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the following name's letters are lined up afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks which college the rapper Eminem, born Marshall Mathers, attended.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshall Mathers is Eminem's real name, which makes 'Marshall' read as a first name; it is the verb marshal (arrange), spelt to complete the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Amherst College is a well-known liberal arts school in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Chooses to run back through memoir of St. Polycarp

indicators.note: running back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left
the answer runs through the words that follow, lying inside them across the word gaps

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of memoir, the word of, St. and the start of Polycarp

explanation.surface: Someone decides to read a saint's memoir backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: St. Polycarp was an early Christian bishop; the saint's name is just camouflage for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt for something is to select it from the alternatives, which is exactly choosing.

clue.text: In Asia, Frank translated a Germanic language

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Frank, working in Asia, renders a text into a Germanic tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a person's name, but its letters join those of Asia as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans grew out of Dutch in southern Africa, placing it in the West Germanic family.

clue.text: Express drama, perhaps overlooking some of the hospital dead

blocks.note: drama is one example of an art
the intensive care unit is one part of a hospital
the late someone is a dead person

explanation.surface: A tense scene where a play's drama looks down on the hospital's dead.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'overlooking' puts the first pieces above, so before, LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to express it clearly in words.

clue.text: 104 independent contractors at the forefront of government

indicators.note: whatever is at the forefront stands at the very front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: 104 in Roman numerals
I is the standard abbreviation for independent
the first letter of contractors

explanation.surface: A hundred and four freelance contractors lead the way in government.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a car, the Honda Civic: one of nine car models hidden in the grid, as 26 Down says.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic describes matters relating to a city, its citizens or its administration, the business of public governance.

clue.text: Pair of Visigoths tallying nuts in a watchful manner

indicators.note: a pair is two, so just the first two letters of the tribe's name are used
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and land in a new order

blocks.note: the first two letters of Visigoths
the letters of tallying, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two Visigoth warriors count their hoard of nuts with a careful eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilant means keeping careful watch for danger, so vigilantly means doing so watchfully.

clue.text: Celebrity to gobble eyeball

blocks.note: a celebrity is a star
to gobble is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A famous person is about to wolf down an eyeball, as on a reality show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyeball' looks like a noun being eaten, but it is the verb meaning to look hard at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to give them a long, hard look, which is staring at them.

clue.text: Cleans fake post office rings

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
PO is the abbreviation for post office
rings are round, like the letter O, so two of them

explanation.surface: A dodgy post office scrubs its rings, perhaps to launder them.
explanation.definitionFit: To shampoo is to wash hair or a carpet with a soapy cleanser.

clue.text: In Guadalajara, two times the appropriate amounts

blocks.note: dos is Spanish for two, and Guadalajara is a Mexican city
times as in eras or ages

explanation.surface: A Mexican note that two times something gives the right quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' looks like multiplication; it is the noun meaning periods, ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured quantity of a medicine to be taken, the amount judged right for the patient.

clue.text: Far from downtown, burn a bus after an accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are wrecked and thrown about, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Out in the outskirts, a bus catches fire after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Downtown is the American word for a city centre. The answer is also the Chevrolet Suburban, one of the nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburban describes the outlying residential districts of a city, away from its centre.

clue.text: War god takes one sign

indicators.note: a word that takes something in holds it inside, so one letter goes into the god's name

blocks.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The god of war receives an omen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the Dodge Aries car, one of the nine in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Stigma surrounds liberal dictator

indicators.note: one word surrounds another by going all the way round it, holding it inside

blocks.note: a stigma is a stain on one's reputation
L is the abbreviation for liberal

explanation.surface: A disgrace clings to a liberal-turned-tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator from the 1920s to 1953.

clue.text: Baldwin turned to suppress insubordinate parts of the brain

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the actor's first name is spelt backwards
to suppress something is to hold it down inside, so one piece is shut within the other

blocks.note: Alec Baldwin is the American actor
an insubordinate person is a rebel

explanation.surface: Alec Baldwin turns to putting down unruly parts of the brain, a dig at the actor's temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Baldwin here is the actor Alec Baldwin, so the word needed is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the region at the back of the brain controlling balance; cerebella is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Grant's alternating current wire

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for alternating current
a cord is an electric wire or flex

explanation.surface: Reads like a note on wiring that belongs to someone named Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant's' looks like a possessive name; it is the verb grant plus 's for is. The answer is also the Honda Accord, one of the nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord someone a privilege is to give or bestow it on them.

clue.text: Braid bread around the east side of Galesburg, Illinois

indicators.note: around means wrapped on all sides, so the bread encloses the next letter
on a map east is the right-hand side, so the last letter of the town is kept

blocks.note: pita is a flat bread
the last letter of Galesburg
IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois

explanation.surface: Instructions to plait a loaf on the east side of a small Illinois town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braid' looks like an instruction to plait the bread, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigtail is a plait of hair hanging from the back of the head, so a braid.

clue.text: Whip up an activity, of course

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom to the top, so backwards

blocks.note: to whip is to flog

explanation.surface: Stirring up some activity, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means played on a course. The answer is also the Volkswagen Golf, one of the nine cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played over a course of holes, so a pursuit that happens on a course.

clue.text: Persistent fashion that's entertaining? Right on

indicators.note: to entertain is to receive guests in, so the stylish word takes the following pair inside it

blocks.note: chic is stylish fashion
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion craze that refuses to fade, and the cry of agreement 'Right on!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right on' looks like a slang cheer, but it splits into R and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic condition is one that lasts a long time or keeps recurring, so persistent.

clue.text: Scattered arcs: nine can be found in the completed diagram

definitions.text: nine can be found in the completed diagram

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about and fall in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Curved lines are strewn about, and nine of something lurk in the filled grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the theme: nine answers are also car models, IMPALA, CHEROKEE, VOLT, LEAF, CIVIC, ARIES, SUBURBAN, ACCORD and GOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine grid answers double as names of automobile models, so the vehicles are what the diagram contains.

clue.text: Engine component is malfunctioning? Fire it (LOL)

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is out of order, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken engine part prompts a joke about sacking it, with LOL for laugh out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed LOL looks like a laughing aside but supplies three letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil filter is the part of a car's engine that strains dirt out of the lubricating oil.

clue.text: Coming in late, Hedda is more adept

indicators.note: someone coming in late misses the start, so the opening letter is lost

blocks.note: Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An actress playing Hedda arrives late and still shows the greater skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedda stands for her surname, as in Ibsen's play Hedda Gabler; missing the start leaves ABLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, so the comparative abler means more skilful.
